security_audit.summary: The 400 presented static matches are false positives caused by documentation syntax, compact JSON, defensive validation, and declared repository orchestration. One medium confidentiality risk remains: approved repository content is transmitted to the external agy provider, and 366 capped static matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/766 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 366 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Repository content is transmitted to an external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Keep per-repository approval mandatory and display a clear transmission notice before every provider launch.

remediation.issue: Driver verification accepts explicit shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Require command preview and approval, use disposable verification copies, and avoid exposing credentials to verifier processes.

remediation.issue: Static review was capped with 366 matches not adjudicated.
remediation.suggestion: Complete an uncapped manual audit of the remaining matches before enabling automatic marketplace publication.

content.user_title: Delegate Repository Work to Google Antigravity
content.value_statement: Large repository tasks can exceed one agent's practical context and execution capacity. This skill delegates bounded work while Codex retains review and verification.
actual_capabilities: Delegates repository exploration, bounded tasks, and project workflows to the agy command-line tool.
Runs edit workflows inside branch-backed disposable Git worktrees.
Supports explicit model selection, effort selection, and compatibility checks.
Tracks multi-cycle jobs with status, wait, continue, restart, cancel, and finalize controls.
Validates worker envelopes and binds driver verification to the current candidate.
Creates isolated verification copies that exclude Git administration data.
limitations: The skill requires Codex CLI, Bash, Python 3, Git, agy, and provider network access.
Repository content may reach Google or Gemini services only after explicit transmission approval.
The packaged workflow supports Codex hosts; Claude and Claude Code hosts are not supported.
Worktrees and filtered environments do not provide complete filesystem, network, or same-user isolation.

use_cases.title: Survey an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Delegate a read-only architecture survey, then verify important paths and commands before reporting.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers joining an existing project

use_cases.title: Implement a bounded change
use_cases.description: Run feature or repair work in a disposable worktree, then review the diff and execute relevant checks.
use_cases.target_user: Codex users handling focused development tasks

use_cases.title: Coordinate a project workflow
use_cases.description: Manage several repair cycles while preserving candidate evidence, approval state, and final assurance.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads coordinating larger repository changes

prompt_templates.title: Explore a repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to map this repository's architecture, entry points, dependencies, and test commands. Request transmission approval before dispatch.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a focused defect
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the task workflow to fix [defect] within [paths]. Review the diff and run [checks] before finalizing.

prompt_templates.title: Backfill tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bulk-test-writer persona for [module]. Restrict edits to test files, then run the repository's selected test command independently.

prompt_templates.title: Run a multi-cycle project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project workflow for [goal] in an isolated worktree. Bind each continuation to driver evidence and report unresolved gaps.

output_examples.input: Explore the service and identify its main entry points and test commands.
output_examples.output: A repository survey listing inspected paths, confirmed entry points, observed test commands, risky areas, and explicit coverage limits.

output_examples.input: Add validation to the upload endpoint and verify the change.
output: A bounded worktree diff covering the requested validation.
Driver-owned check results tied to the current candidate.
A verified, partially verified, rejected, or blocked final disposition.

output_examples.input: Complete a larger refactor with repair cycles.
output_examples.output: A preserved candidate with lifecycle status, diff review evidence, check summaries, unresolved gaps, and an explicit final assurance.

best_practices: Obtain explicit approval for the exact repository scope before every first provider transmission.
Use disposable worktrees and keep controller state outside the delegated repository.
Review every diff and run driver-selected checks without trusting worker command claims.
anti_patterns: Do not send credentials, private keys, unrelated files, raw logs, or controller state to the provider.
Do not execute commands or tests reported by the worker envelope.
Do not commit, push, publish, install tools, or bypass permissions without separate approval.

faq.question: What does this skill delegate?
faq.answer: It delegates repository exploration, focused implementation, test backfills, and larger project workflows to agy.

faq.question: Does it send repository data externally?
faq.answer: Yes. Approved task and readable repository content may reach Google or Gemini services through agy.

faq.question: Does it verify worker results automatically?
faq.answer: It validates envelopes and evidence bindings, but Codex must review diffs and run relevant checks.

faq.question: Can it modify my main checkout?
faq.answer: Edit workflows should use a branch-backed disposable worktree, not the main checkout.

faq.question: Can it use Claude or Claude Code hosts?
faq.answer: No. The packaged instructions identify Codex as the supported host.

faq.question: Does the worktree provide a security sandbox?
faq.answer: No. It isolates workflow state but does not fully isolate filesystem, network, credentials, or same-user processes.
